messages:
support_ella: FYI — multiple customer escalations hitting us with 504s on /v1/generate (hosted). Started ~2026-03-15T12:03Z. Customers report retries make it worse. Links to tickets: T-4421, T-4422.

sre_ahmad: seeing the same from infra alerts. SLO alert fired for gateway-ingress 5xx > 0.5% over 10m.

ops-bot: ALERT: slo_ingress_5xx_rate > threshold (0.62%) — fired at 2026-03-15T12:07Z.

ingrid: dashboard -> https://console.redwood.local/slo/ingress (use the prod region selector). p50 OK, p99 token latency spiked and 5xx rate climbs.

support_ella: quick customer repro: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-2.7b","input":"hello"}' — response is HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout after ~30s.

sre_ahmad: grabbing logs. Early look: upstream timeouts with error message "upstream read timeout" and a mix of 522/504/502. Two patterns: long-tail requests hitting large context lengths, and a second cohort with short requests that time out in the gateway before reaching runtime.

sre_ahmad: running a quick log query (Kibana):

```
service:gateway AND path:"/v1/generate" AND status:[500 TO 599]
| stats count() by upstream_host, status, response_time, model_name
| sort - response_time desc
```

sre_ahmad: results show a handful of backend hosts with elevated error ratios and response_time > 20s. upstream_host=runtime-cc-47 appears frequently.

tracing-bot: sample traces for 504 requests show missing downstream spans in ~40% of traces — looks like the gateway times out before the runtime reports back; gap between gateway span end and runtime span start.

ingrid: that trace gap smells like a tcp reset or LB-level conn issue. Can someone check ingress ELB metrics for connection resets and active connections?

devex_sam: also seeing auth failures in a small subset — 401s correlate with a billing service outage earlier; I think two issues are coinciding. We should separate auth/billing 401s from pure 5xx/timeouts.

support_ella: customers noted first 401s then 504s in some traces. Escalation ticket asks for short-term mitigation and ETA.

sre_ahmad: immediate triage plan: 1) identify and cordon suspected runtime hosts with high error rates; 2) temporary increase gateway upstream timeout from 30s -> 60s for /v1/generate rule to avoid client 504s for long-context workloads; 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model (rwd-2.7b-fallback) for hosts failing healthchecks.

product_maya: be careful with global timeout change — could mask real backend degradation and increase queueing. Only do region-scoped change if we confirm hosts flapping.

sre_ahmad: agreed. I'll scope to us-west-2 for now.

ingrid: healthcheck snapshots:
```
ELB.ConnReset[us-west-2][12:00-12:10] -> +350% (baseline)
ELB.ActiveConn[us-west-2] -> +12%
Runtime.healthcheck_failures(runtime-cc-47) -> 21 failures / 10m
```

sre_ahmad: cordoning runtime-cc-47 from traffic now (mark unhealthy in lb).

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: route-rule update applied to gateway (region us-west-2) by sre_ahmad at 2026-03-15T12:18Z — upstream timeout increased to 60s for /v1/generate.

support_ella: customers on call confirm immediate improvement for some requests, but a subset still seeing 504s ~> investigating.

tracing-bot: after route change, traces show some longer tail completions (40–50s) succeeding, but a persistent cohort of requests with no runtime spans — those still 504.

devex_sam: repro steps for the persistent cohort: send concurrent small requests (n=50 qps) with short input -> gateway returns 504 within ~2s. That pattern points to authentication/middleware failing fast.

sre_ahmad: pulling gateway logs for those quick-504s. Found entries: "auth-service: upstream 401 -> gateway abort" immediately followed by "gateway: responding 504 due to no response from runtime" — odd ordering.

support_ella: could be a race where auth service returns 401 then a later component mis-classifies as 504. Examples: customer A logs attached: 
```
[12:05:12] request_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate auth_check=401 auth_token=billing_error
[12:05:12] gateway: forward to runtime_id=runtime-cc-52 start
[12:05:14] gateway: timeout waiting for runtime -> 504
```

sre_ahmad: that ordering means some requests are double-processed: auth indicates failure but gateway still forwards the request (race). I suspect the async auth cache/queue has lag. Check auth-cache TTL and sync loop.

ingrid: also verifying K/V cache saturation — our prefix/KV cache metrics show spikes in cache misses for model rwd-5b in us-west-2 around the window. Miss storms can cause a rush to runtime and overload a subset of hosts.

devex_sam: mitigation idea: enable request-level admission control for incoming bursts (throttle at 200 rps per model per region) and enable cold-cache circuit breaker (return 429 on cache-miss storms). Would reduce overload while we fix hosts.

support_ella: customers prefer not to get 429s — but they accept a temporary throttle if we give ETA. We should coordinate comms.

sre_ahmad: action items assigned: 
- sre_ahmad: continue cordon and rotate affected runtime hosts; check out-of-memory / oom-kill logs on runtime-cc-47 and runtime-cc-52.
- ingrid: investigate ELB conn resets and K/V cache miss root cause, collect graphs.
- devex_sam: prepare fallback routing plan and a short-lived throttle policy; prepare sample config for API gateway.
- support_ella: update customer tickets with mitigation steps and ETA (30–45m).

product_maya: start incident Slack channel #incident-2069876543 and give customer facing note draft.

support_ella: FYI draft for customer: "We're seeing a transient runtime overload + gateway timeouts in us-west-2 that is causing intermittent 5xx/504s. We're rotating impacted hosts, applying temporary routing/timeouts, and expect normal service within an hour. We'll send an update in 30 minutes."

tracing-bot: follow-up: root cause hypothesis: cache miss storm -> overloaded runtime hosts -> conn resets from ELB -> gateway timeouts. Still investigating auth/billing 401 coupling.

sre_ahmad: quick checks on runtime-cc-47 logs show repeated 'OOMKilled' and 'kernel: conn reset by peer' around 12:04-12:12Z. Opening host-repro ticket: H-9923.

ingrid: I'll pull request flows and add Grafana links: 
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ingress/5xx-over-time?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2
- KV cache dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cache/kv-miss-storms

devex_sam: sample gateway config snippet to apply if we need fast rollback: 
```
- match: path: /v1/generate
  timeout: 60s
  retry_policy: none
  fallback: route: /fallback/rwd-2.7b
  admission_control: {max_rps: 200}
```

support_ella: leaving notes in tickets. Will wait for infra rotation + caches to settle.

sre_ahmad: will post another update after host rotation and ELB checks (~12:45Z). Marking this thread incident-critical.

support_ella: thanks all — please ping on-call if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT: channel #incident-2069876543 created by product_maya at 2026-03-15T12:25Z.

sre_ahmad: update at 12:40Z: rotated 3 hosts, runtime error rate dropped 70%, gateway 5xx rate down to 0.18% in us-west-2. Continuing post-incident analysis for cache and auth race.

support_ella: customers notified. Closing urgent escalation, leaving incident open for RCA.

product_maya: assigning RCA owners: infra (hosts/OOM), infra-net (ELB resets), platform (kv-cache), auth (billing coupling)."
